title: The noesis testnet walk
purpose: Two testers who follow this walk exercise the same protocol. Every write the app can send is either a numbered step here or is listed under outOfWalk with the reason it cannot be reached on a testnet — tools/validate-walk.mjs proves that, against the app source, on every run.

roles.operator: holds the protocol owner key. On a fresh testnet this is whoever ran the deploy; the act-O steps are the only ones that need it.
roles.creator: launches a collection. Needs testnet ETH, an image, and nothing else — no allowlist and no prior standing.
roles.collector: buys, mints, bids, stakes. Needs testnet ETH only. This is the role most testers should walk first.
roles.artist: holds the overlay-module role on a collection whose art is published in waves. Reached on a collection whose overlay module was wired at launch in C-1.

blockingRule: A step marked blocking:true is one whose failure stops a launch — money moves wrongly, or a person cannot complete a thing the app offered them. A failure on any step is filed as a noesis row either way; blocking says whether the row is allowed to stay open when the launch button is pressed.

operator: the wallet that owns the protocol on the chain you are walking — the address that ran the deploy
enough test ETH for about twenty transactions
the deployed addresses, which the app already carries for the chain it was built against
creator: a wallet with test ETH — enough to seed a pool, so ask for more than a faucet's default drip
one image file to launch with, under a few megabytes
nothing else: no allowlist, no approval, no prior standing
collector: a wallet with test ETH — a single faucet drip is enough for act B
a collection that is already live, which act C produces; if nobody has walked C yet, walk it first or ask for the address of one that has
artist: the overlay-module role on a live collection, which the creator grants during act C

report.destination: Reply to the post you were invited from. That is the channel the invite came down, and it is where a reply is read.
report.secondary: The app's own /board is public, permissionless and on-chain, so a report posted there is one anybody can read back. One trap: the feed shows only posts whose attached value clears the registry's postThreshold. The in-app composer defaults the amount to the live threshold, so post through the composer rather than by hand and your report will be visible.
include: the step id — every finding is filed against one, and a finding with no step id is a finding nobody can walk back to
what you did, in the words you would use to do it again
what you expected, which is the step's own expect line, not your guess at it
what happened instead, with the screen you were on
the transaction hash if the wallet got as far as sending one, and the wallet's own error if it did not
the chain id and the address of MasterRegistryV1 the invite printed, so the run can be told from any other run

acts.title: the operator arms the protocol
acts.note: Most of these are executed by the deploy script rather than by hand. Walk them anyway: the panel is the surface an operator will actually use six months from now, when the script is gone and the state is live.

steps.title: register the factories and the vault kinds
steps.given: a fresh deploy, connected as the protocol owner
steps.do: in the master-registry panel, register each deployed factory address and each vault implementation
steps.expect: each one appears in the panel's own list afterwards, and /launch offers the newly registered kind

steps.title: set the launch economics
steps.given: the factories are registered
steps.do: in the platform-config panel, set each value, then reload the page. The bonding fee is in basis points and the contract refuses anything above 300 — try 400 first and the button stays disabled with the ceiling named, rather than sending a transaction that reverts
steps.expect: every value reads back the number that was set — not a default, and not the previous value

steps.title: price the featured queue
steps.given: the featured queue manager is deployed
steps.do: set the daily rate, the decay, the min/max duration and the queue size
steps.expect: the price a collector is quoted in B-12 matches the rate set here

steps.title: curate an alignment target
steps.given: a token address to align to — on a testnet, any ERC-20 the operator can mint
steps.do: register the target, then edit it, then point its community payout at an address you control
steps.expect: the target appears at /target/:id with the payout address it was given, and /launch offers it as an alignment choice

steps.title: judge a target request
steps.given: B-15 has been walked, so at least two requests are pending
steps.do: approve one and reject the other
steps.expect: the approved token becomes an alignment choice; the rejected one does not, and its requester can take the deposit back in B-15

steps.title: approve a component, then revoke it
steps.given: a deployed module address (the merkle gating module will do)
steps.do: approve it, confirm a creator can select it in C-6, then revoke it
steps.expect: after revocation the module is no longer offered to a creator, and a collection already using it keeps working

steps.title: delegate an agent, then take it back
steps.given: a second address to act as the agent
steps.do: set the agent, name an emergency revoker, then revoke the agent
steps.expect: the agent address can act while set and cannot after revocation

steps.title: revoke a collection, and correct one that is wrong
steps.given: at least two launched collections from act C
steps.do: correct one collection's metadata pointer, then revoke the other
steps.expect: the corrected collection renders its new art; the revoked one disappears from /collections and from every listing, and its own page says why

steps.title: retire a factory and a vault kind
steps.given: collections already launched from that factory
steps.do: deactivate one factory and one vault kind
steps.expect: /launch stops offering them, and every collection already launched from them still loads and still trades

steps.title: de-curate a target that is already carrying money
steps.given: a target with at least one aligned collection that has taken fees
steps.do: deactivate the target
steps.expect: no new collection can align to it, and the money already accrued to it can still be sent to its community payout

steps.title: sweep the treasury
steps.given: the treasury holds a protocol cut from act B, and (for the token legs) any ERC-20/ERC-721 sent to it
steps.do: withdraw each of the three
steps.expect: the destination balance rises by the amount the panel said, to the wei

steps.title: price the target-request queue
steps.given: the alignment panel is reachable, and at least one request has been submitted in B-15 so the queue is not empty
steps.do: in the alignment panel's request-queue rows, set the deposit, the maximum number of pending requests, and the TTL in days. Then reload, and submit a request as the collector in B-15 against the new numbers
steps.expect: each row reads back what was set — the deposit in ETH, the count, and the TTL rendered in days rather than seconds. A submission escrows the new deposit, and one past the new maximum is refused by the contract rather than accepted and stranded

steps.title: appoint an ambassador, then take the seat back
steps.given: a curated alignment target from O-4, and a second wallet address to appoint
steps.do: in the alignment panel's ambassador row, add the address against the target id. Have that wallet walk H-2. Then remove it and have the same wallet try H-2 again
steps.expect: the appointed wallet can edit the target in H-2 and the removed one cannot — the edit is refused by the contract rather than accepted and ignored. The seat survives de-curation: after O-10 the ambassador can still edit the description, and only the spending is frozen

acts.title: a creator launches and runs a collection
acts.note: Walk C-1 at minimum. C-2 and C-3 are the other two families and each one changes what acts B and H can reach.

steps.title: launch an ERC-404 bonding collection
steps.given: testnet ETH and an image
steps.do: walk the wizard end to end and send the deploy
steps.expect: the wizard's quoted cost is what the wallet asks for; on success it lands on the collection's own page, reachable again from /collections

steps.title: launch an ERC-1155 edition collection
steps.given: the same
steps.do: pick the edition family and deploy with at least one edition
steps.expect: the collection page shows the edition, and its mint button is offered only once the edition has opened

steps.title: launch an ERC-721 auction collection
steps.given: the same
steps.do: pick the auction family and deploy
steps.expect: the collection page shows an empty auction queue, and C-9 is offered

steps.title: ask for a yield vault at launch
steps.given: an alignment target from O-4 with no vault of the kind you want
steps.do: request the vault from the wizard's alignment step
steps.expect: the wizard says the vault is pending rather than pretending it exists, and the launch can still complete

steps.title: schedule the curve, then arm it
steps.given: your own ERC-404 collection from C-1
steps.do: set an open time a few minutes out and a maturity after it, arm bonding, and try to buy before the open time
steps.expect: the buy is not offered before the open time — the app refuses it rather than letting the chain revert it — and becomes available on its own once the time passes; a maturity at or before the open time is refused in the form, not on-chain

steps.title: gate a mint behind an allowlist
steps.given: a collection of yours and a list of addresses, one of them the collector's
steps.do: configure the gate from the creator panel
steps.expect: the listed address can mint and an unlisted one is told it is not on the list before it spends gas

steps.title: dress the collection and fix its art pointer
steps.given: a launched collection
steps.do: change the style, then repoint the metadata URI to a different image
steps.expect: both changes render on the collection page and on its card in /collections without a hard reload

steps.title: add an edition, give it a free allocation, then correct it
steps.given: your ERC-1155 collection from C-2
steps.do: add a second edition, set a free allocation on it, then edit its metadata
steps.expect: the new edition is listed and mintable at its own /:chainId/:slug/edition/:id, and the free allocation is what B-8 draws from

steps.title: queue a piece for auction
steps.given: your ERC-721 collection from C-3
steps.do: queue a piece with a reserve
steps.expect: the auction starts and the page shows a running clock a bidder can act against

steps.title: take the creator's share out
steps.given: editions have been minted in B-7
steps.do: withdraw from the creator panel
steps.expect: the wallet receives what the panel said was withdrawable, and the panel then reads zero

steps.title: claim every fee stream a creator has
steps.given: trading and minting have happened on each family
steps.do: claim from each family's creator panel
steps.expect: the amount claimed matches what was displayed, and a second claim with nothing owed is refused with a reason rather than burning gas

steps.title: retry a vault contribution that failed
steps.given: a collection whose alignment vault was unreachable when a sale settled — reachable by aligning to a target whose vault is deactivated in O-9
steps.do: retry from the creator panel
steps.expect: the pending figure falls to zero and the vault receives it; the retry is reconcilable from the events, not only from the number on screen

steps.title: move a collection to a different vault
steps.given: two registered vaults for the same target
steps.do: migrate on each family
steps.expect: fees accrued before the migration are not stranded — they reach one of the two vaults and the page says which

steps.title: hand a collection to an agent
steps.given: the agent address from O-7
steps.do: delegate on each family, then act as the agent
steps.expect: the agent reaches exactly the controls the panel said it would, and nothing that moves the creator's money

steps.title: graduate the curve
steps.given: the curve from C-1 bought out to its graduation point in B-1
steps.do: deploy liquidity, then activate staking
steps.expect: the collection page swaps the curve panel for the graduated-venue panel of B-6, names the venue it deployed to, and staking becomes available in B-5

steps.title: get the deploy bond back
steps.given: a bonded launch that met its condition
steps.do: claim the refund from the creator panel
steps.expect: the bond returns in full, and the panel is honest about the deadline it was measured against

steps.title: sweep the surplus a fee claim leaves behind
steps.given: an ERC-404 collection from C-1 that has been traded in B-1 and whose fees were claimed in C-11
steps.do: in the creator admin panel, read the sweep-surplus row and press it
steps.expect: the row names the amount that backs neither a sell refund nor a staker, and the sweep pays exactly that. With nothing above those two reserves the button is disabled and says so, instead of sending a transaction the contract reverts. Selling back in B-1 after the sweep still pays out in full — the sweep must never have touched the sell reserve

steps.title: re-send a vault cut that never landed, on both families that strand one
steps.given: an ERC-721 auction collection from C-3 with an auction settled in B-9, and a graduated ERC-404 collection from C-15 — both aligned to a vault
steps.do: in the auction collection's creator admin panel, read the stranded-tithe row and press flush if it names an amount. Then do the same on the ERC-404 collection, whose row sends the same call against the liquidity module it graduated through rather than against the instance. If either says nothing is stranded, say so in the row — that is the expected reading when every settlement delivered
steps.expect: a stranded amount leaves for the vault and the row falls to nothing stranded, on whichever family had one. With nothing stranded the button is disabled rather than reverting. The call is permissionless on both, so it works from a wallet that owns nothing — walk it once from the creator and once from the collector wallet

steps.title: pull the endowment yield, vest the principal, deliver the community share
steps.given: a collection on an endowment vault — C-4 asked for one at launch — with yield harvested into it in B-11
steps.do: on the collection page, open the community-endowment panel. Press claim yield as the collection owner, then look at it again from a wallet that is not the owner. Press vest once the vest window has elapsed and principal is still escrowed, and deliver community share when one is shown as undelivered
steps.expect: the claim pays the owner and the accrued figure falls to zero; from any other wallet the claim button is not on the page at all, rather than present and reverting. Vest moves the matured principal into the community corpus and ends this collection's accrual, which the panel says before it is pressed. The delivery is disabled while no community payout is wired, and names that as the reason

acts.title: a collector uses the thing
acts.note: This act is the one a stranger walks. It needs no key and no standing — only testnet ETH and the link.

steps.title: buy on the curve, then sell back
steps.given: an armed, open ERC-404 collection from C-5
steps.do: buy for a small amount, watch the holdings panel, then sell part of it back
steps.expect: the coin balance and the NFTs both move in the same transaction; the quote shown before signing is what settles, within the slippage stated on screen

steps.title: claim a free mint on the curve
steps.given: a collection launched with a free allocation
steps.do: claim it, then try to claim a second time
steps.expect: the first claim lands; the second is refused before it is signed, and an exhausted pool says it is claimed out rather than offering a claim

steps.title: trade up and down the tiers
steps.given: enough coin from B-1 to reach a tier above the base
steps.do: mint up a tier, mint back down, then claim what the down-trade released
steps.expect: the escrow released is claimable and arrives; the tier art changes on both moves

steps.title: reroll a piece, and stop receiving them
steps.given: at least two NFTs from B-1
steps.do: reroll one, then turn skip-NFT on and buy again
steps.expect: the rerolled piece changes; with skip on, a buy moves coin and mints no NFT

steps.title: stake, earn, unstake
steps.given: staking activated in C-15
steps.do: stake, wait for a reward to accrue, claim it, then unstake everything
steps.expect: the reward claimed matches what was displayed; unstaking returns the full stake

steps.title: trade the graduated token without leaving the site
steps.given: a graduated collection from C-15. Which router runs is set by the venue it graduated to — Uni-V4 and ZAMM go through zRouter, the Cypher family through the Algebra router — so walk this once per venue you can reach and record which one you actually traded.
steps.do: buy with ETH, then approve and sell back to ETH
steps.expect: the sell settles in native ETH, not in a wrapped token; the min-out shown before signing is a separate figure from the amount you receive, and the receipt lands between them

steps.title: mint an edition
steps.given: an open edition from C-2
steps.do: mint one, then mint several in one transaction, with a message attached
steps.expect: the cost quoted is what is charged; the message appears in the collection's feed

steps.title: claim a free edition
steps.given: the free allocation set in C-8
steps.do: claim, then attempt a second claim
steps.expect: as B-2 — the second is refused before signing, and an exhausted allocation says so

steps.title: bid, win, settle — and lose
steps.given: a running auction from C-9, and a second wallet to bid against
steps.do: bid, be outbid, bid again near the end to trigger the time extension, let it end, settle it. Separately, let an auction with no bids expire and reclaim the piece.
steps.expect: the outbid wallet gets its ETH back without asking; the extension is visible on the clock; settlement delivers the piece and pays the creator; the unsold piece returns to the creator

steps.title: unlock the art overlay on a piece you hold
steps.given: a piece from B-1 on a collection with an overlay module and a published wave from H-1
steps.do: unlock the commission, unlock a specific wave, then select which wave the piece wears
steps.expect: the price paid is the one the panel quoted; the piece renders the selected wave everywhere it appears, not only on this page

steps.title: harvest the alignment vault
steps.given: an aligned collection whose vault has accrued yield
steps.do: harvest from the vault panel
steps.expect: the yield reaches the community payout set in O-4, and the panel does not claim a principal is fully vested while a tranche clock is still running

steps.title: rent the featured slot
steps.given: the queue priced in O-3
steps.do: rent a slot, boost it above another, renew it, then let one expire and prune it
steps.expect: the price charged is the price quoted; the home page's featured row reflects each move; an expired slot leaves the row

steps.title: post to the board
steps.given: the post threshold set in O-2
steps.do: on /board, add several posts to the cart, then send them together from the cart bar
steps.expect: the fee charged matches the number of posts; every post appears in the feed it was addressed to

steps.title: set a profile, then clear it
steps.given: a connected wallet
steps.do: set a name and avatar, check it renders on a collection you touched, then clear it
steps.expect: the name replaces the raw address everywhere it was showing, and clearing puts the address back

steps.title: ask for an alignment target, and take the deposit back
steps.given: the deposit amount set at deploy, and a token address to propose
steps.do: submit two requests, have O-5 approve one and reject the other, then withdraw the refund on the rejected one
steps.expect: the deposit is taken at submit and returned in full on the rejected request; the approved one's deposit is accounted for where the page says it goes

steps.title: deliver the community's accrued fees
steps.given: a vault whose target carries the community payout address set in O-4, with fees accrued to it by the trading in B-1
steps.do: open the vault from /vaults and press deliver — the button sends flushTargetFees on an endowment vault and withdrawTargetFees on a Cypher, ZAMM or Uni one, so walk whichever kind the deploy has and say which in the row
steps.expect: the waiting amount falls to zero and the payout address receives it; with no payout address set the button is disabled and says the delivery is waiting on one, rather than sending a transaction that reverts

steps.title: release the vested corpus to the community
steps.given: an endowment vault reached in B-16 whose corpus has vested — the Cypher, ZAMM and Uni families do not offer this and their panel does not show the control
steps.do: press release, then press it a second time with nothing left to release
steps.expect: the first release sends the deployable corpus to the payout address; the second is refused by a disabled button that says no vested corpus is left, not by a revert

steps.title: deliver the protocol's accrued cut
steps.given: a Uni, ZAMM or Cypher vault that has taken trading fees — the same vault B-16 delivers the community share from
steps.do: open the vault from /vaults and press deliver on the protocol-cut section
steps.expect: the undelivered figure falls to zero and the treasury the vault was wired with receives it. The call takes no destination, so pressing it from a stranger's wallet sends the money to the same place — walk it from a wallet that owns nothing and check the treasury balance, not the sender's. With nothing accrued the section is not on the page at all

steps.title: expire your own stale target request and get the deposit back
steps.given: a request submitted in B-15 that the operator has neither approved nor rejected, and a TTL set in O-12 short enough to elapse during the walk
steps.do: on /request-target, find the request under your own requests and press expire & refund. Then claim the refund with the row B-15 already walks
steps.expect: the button appears only once the TTL has elapsed on a still-pending request — before that there is no button, not a disabled one. After it, the request leaves the pending queue and the deposit is claimable. It is permissionless, so a second wallet can expire the same request and the refund still goes to whoever submitted it

acts.title: the roles a collection hands out
acts.note: These are reachable only after act C has created the standing they need. They are the surfaces most likely to be walked by nobody, which is why they are numbered.

steps.title: publish a wave of art, price it, and let it auto-apply
steps.given: an ERC-404 collection with an overlay module wired, connected as its artist
steps.do: publish a wave, set the unlock commission, then turn auto-latest on and publish a second wave
steps.expect: holders can reach the wave in B-10; with auto-latest on, a piece that has not chosen a wave shows the newest one

steps.title: an ambassador edits the target they were given
steps.given: an ambassador address added to a target by the operator
steps.do: connect as the ambassador and edit the target from its own page
steps.expect: the ambassador reaches the edit form and no owner-only control; after the target is de-curated in O-10, the ambassador can still operate what exists and cannot deploy anything new

steps.title: a community moves its own payout
steps.given: the address O-4 pointed the community payout at, connected as that address, on a vault bound to that target
steps.do: open the vault, find the move-payout row under the payout address, enter a second address you control and send it; then connect as the FIRST address again and confirm the row is gone, and as the operator confirm /admin offers no way to move it either
steps.expect: the payout moves to the second address and the deliver button in B-16 then pays there; the row shows only to whoever is currently receiving the payout, so the first address loses it the moment it moves and the operator never had it. This is the one authority in the walk the protocol cannot exercise on a community's behalf: the operator pins a payout once in O-4 and can never move it, which is why the row lives here and not on /admin.

outOfWalk.why: /exec404 trades CULT EXECUTIVES, a mainnet contract this protocol did not deploy. There is no testnet counterpart to trade, so nothing on that page can be walked on a deployed testnet.
the allowance leg of the same /exec404 trade — see zRouterAbi.swapV2.
an EXEC404 contract call on /exec404 — see zRouterAbi.swapV2.
an EXEC404 contract call on /exec404 — see zRouterAbi.swapV2.
an EXEC404 mirror call on /exec404 — see zRouterAbi.swapV2.

blindSpots.why: the abi is picked at runtime from a FACTORY table, so the scan cannot pair it. It is an estimateContractGas read, not a write, and the write it estimates is covered by C-1/C-2/C-3.

the abi is picked at runtime from the venue the collection graduated to — one of three liquidity deployer modules — so the scan cannot pair it. The write is flushPendingVaultCut on whichever module holds the stranded cut; it is walked as C-18 on the auction family, and the ERC-404 row beside it sends the same call against the module instead of the instance.
